request.spec:
A steward can roll the year over: a year entry and a button. It generates the next fiscal year's
twelve periods exactly as the fiscal year generator does, and for each person their open figure at
the end of the old year's last period (the due of their claims that count, belonging to a period of
the old year, OPEN or PENDING at that period's end) is added to their carried figure for the new
year's first period as OPENING_SET lines; then ROLLOVER fy=<old FY> periods=<made> is written. A year
with no periods, anyone but a steward, or a bad year is refused with an error.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can roll the year over: a year entry and a button. It generates the next fiscal year's
twelve periods exactly as the fiscal year generator does, and for each person their open figure at
the end of the old year's last period (the due of their claims that count, belonging to a period of
the old year, OPEN or PENDING at that period's end) is added to their carried figure for the new
year's first period as OPENING_SET lines; then ROLLOVER fy=<old FY> periods=<made> is written. A year
with no periods, anyone but a steward, or a bad year is refused with an error.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Year-end rollover is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 specs (the main rollover test and scenarios 1–3).

**What a steward can now do:** the Periods panel has a year box and a "Roll year over" button. On success it shows how many periods it made. Otherwise it shows a refusal message. Pressing it for, say, 2026:
1. Generates fiscal year 2027's twelve periods through the existing fiscal-year generator, so the same `PERIOD_ADDED` lines are written.
2. Works out each person's open figure: the due of their claims whose due-by falls in a 2026 period and that were OPEN or PENDING at the end of 2026's last period. It counts due the same way the existing carried figure does.
3. Adds that figure to each person's opening balance for the new year's first period, writing an `OPENING_SET` line per person.
4. Writes `ROLLOVER fy=FY2026 periods=<made>`.

It is refused, and nothing is written, when the year isn't a valid YYYY, the user isn't a steward, or that fiscal year has no periods.

**Changes:**
- **Server:** a new `period/RolloverService.java`, a new `Rollup.openByPerson(...)` for the open figure, and a `POST /api/sheets/{id}/periods/rollover` endpoint in `PeriodController`. No schema change was needed because openings are already stored on periods.
- **Front end:** `Periods.rollover()` in `core/periods.ts`, and the form in `features/periods/periods.ts` with the `rollover-year`, `rollover`, `rollover-made` and `rollover-error` test ids.

**Decisions the request left open:**
- **Zero figures:** a person whose open figure is 0.00 gets no `OPENING_SET` line. The test only covers people with non-zero figures, so writing a 0.00 line instead would also pass it.
- **Which periods count:** a period belongs to the old year if its from-date falls inside it. The "first period" of the new year is the earliest one whose from-date falls inside the new year.
- **Periods that already exist:** the `periods=` count is however many the generator actually made. If some of the new year's periods already existed, that will be fewer than 12, and the openings still go onto the new year's first period.

The test helpers also reference a `rollover-undo` button. The request doesn't ask for undo and no test uses it, so I didn't build it.
